key_insight: A locally deployable small language model can perform case-level and trio-based genomic interpretation by combining ACMG/AMP evidence assignment with inheritance reasoning and deterministic checks.
clinical_relevance: This could enable privacy-preserving variant interpretation on hospital infrastructure, supporting more complete genomic reporting without relying on cloud-based models.
method: Benchmarked 13 small language models on 150 genetics multiple-choice questions and selected Qwen3.5-9B.
Built a four-stage IVA pipeline that assigns ACMG/AMP criteria, applies inheritance logic, and generates structured reports.
Used deterministic code for retrieval, phasing, scoring, citation checking, and formatting.
evidence_signal: IVA was evaluated on synthetic scenarios, 16 solved trios, and 327 solved singleton visual impairment cases, recovering 100% of trio variants of interest and 93% of causative singleton variants.
watch_item: Precision was modest and failures included omission, unverified mechanism claims, reasoning-to-label mismatches, and arithmetic errors, so human review remains essential.
paper_title: IVA, a locally deployable Intelligent Variant Analyser based on a small language model for complete case-level and trio-based genomic interpretation.
